newsitem.title: USA: Dollar Financial to issue $100 million in debt.
newsitem.headline: Dollar Financial to issue $100 million in debt.

text.p: Dollar Financial Group Inc, the second largest chain of check-cashing stores in the U.S., is in the process of raising $100 million through a 144a private placement offering of junk bonds, market sources said.

The offering, which sources say will represent the first junk deal by a check cashing company, will consist of $100 million in senior notes due 2006. Lehman Brothers and BA Securities Inc will serve as underwriters.
Lehman Brothers is currently conducting a road show for the offering, which is expected to end this Friday. The deal is expected to price soon after, the sources added.
Price talk was not yet available.
Lehman and BA Securities officials declined to comment.

According to a preliminary prospectus obtained by Reuters, Dollar plans to use proceeds from the offering to pay $71.4 million in debt under an exisiting credit facility. Proceeds will also be used to complete acquisitions of other check cashing companies.
The company will enter into a new $25 million revolving credit facility in connection with the completion of the offering, according to the prospectus.
Dollar, which is privately held, operates a network of 426 stores in 14 states, the District of Columbia and Canada.

The stores, which operate under local brand names such as ABC Check Cashing and Almost-A-Banc, charge fees to cash checks and money orders. Some locations also serve as distribution centers for public assistance.
Dollar's primary customers are lower-income individuals, who require basic consumer financial services and are under-served by traditional retail banking networks, according to the prospectus.
Dollar officials did not return calls seeking comment.

Seperately, market sources say Ace Cash Express Inc, the largest check cashing chain in the U.S., is in the process of raising $20 million through a private debt offering through Montgomery Securities. No confirmation was immediately available.
